question: Add faith sponsors outside the top-50 frame (WaterStone/Christian Community Foundation, NCF affiliates such as NCF Wisconsin and NCF Real Property, Catholic Community Foundation of Minnesota, other Jewish community foundations) by reading their FY2023-24 Schedule I lines, and re-estimate the faith-sponsor share of church DAF dollars
conclusion_affected: Faith sponsors send 22.1% of top-50 church-block dollars; the top-50 frame contains only seven faith sponsors, so the faith share of all DAF dollars to churches is likely understated
rationale: In the block, faith sponsors' church share is 2.2x their share of all top-50 dollars (22.1% vs 10.0%), and Servant Foundation and Thrivent send about 40% of their own dollars to it. Faith sponsors below rank 50 are not in the numerator at all

question: Split the 'church' FOUNDATION 10 block into congregations versus church-coded ministries, schools and denominational bodies with a hand-coded random sample of 300 (stratified by DAF dollars), to replace the name-rule classifier
conclusion_affected: Only 52.2% of block dollars go to recipients whose names read as congregations; ministries (Cru, Wycliffe, Salvation Army), Catholic and LDS bodies and church schools hold the rest
rationale: FOUNDATION 10 is the IRS 170(b)(1)(A)(i) code, which covers conventions, associations and integrated auxiliaries, not only congregations. The name rules leave 10.4% of dollars unclassified and mislabel some (e.g. FOCUS as a congregation)

question: Finish the P-B41N15-01 giving-page check: search websites for the 10 sampled congregations not searched, retry the 5 robots-unreadable hosts once, and extend to a second seeded draw of 50 so that n of scanned pages reaches about 30
conclusion_affected: 0 of 14 scanned congregation pages show any DAF option, versus 40.3% of top-300 recipient donate pages; n=14 is too small for a stable rate
rationale: Only 21 of 40 searched congregations had a site named in search results, 5 had unreadable robots.txt and 2 were unreachable; the 95% Wilson interval on 0/14 runs to 21.5%

question: Confirm megachurch legal names for the Outreach 100 2023-24 churches that did not match (35 of 107) from each church's own site footer or state corporate registry, and recompute the megachurch share of church DAF dollars
conclusion_affected: Strict name matching puts 54 Outreach 100 churches at 2.2% of block dollars (4.3% of congregation dollars); legal names that differ from brand names are missed
rationale: Life.Church (Life Covenant Church Inc, $29.7m) is only a loose match; Dream City, Eleven22 and LCBC did not match at all

question: Test whether Schedule I's $5,000 per-recipient threshold hides more church dollars than other sectors: compare sponsor-published religion grant counts and dollars (Fidelity Charitable Giving Report, JCF NY Giving Report) with Schedule I religion lines for the same sponsor-year
conclusion_affected: Church grant lines have a 10th percentile of $6,224, close to the $5,000 threshold; the block's dollar total may be understated more than the repo's ~2% overall
rationale: Fidelity reports religion at 27% of grant count but 13.1% of dollars, so small grants matter more for churches
